16. The respondent No.2 filed Affidavit-in-opposition and denied the statements and material allegations made in the writ petition and stated that a plot being No. 16 consisting of 1.00 acre Khas land was given permanent lease to the petitioner and a lease agreement was signed on 4.7.2005 with some terms and condition. As per clause 11 of the terms of the lease agreement 'the construction work of the hotel/motel has to be beginning within one year from taking possession of the property and have to be completed within three years'. Though possession of the plot was handed over to the petitioner on 29.01.2006 but the petitioner has failed to complete construction work within stipulated time. As per clause 11 of the terms and condition of the lease agreement nothing is allowed to be constructed in the plot except Hotel/Motel. It is also stated that the lessee has submitted a written undertaking in stamp of Taka 150/-that he will be bound to follow the conditions of lease agreement. In clause 18 of the lease agreement, it was provided that `if any condition of the lease agreement is violated by the lessee in that case lesser has been authorized to cancel the agreement by his own decision'. In clause 19 of the lease agreement, it was provided that' if any condition is violated by the lessee in that case the agreement shall be treated as cancelled and the property will come to the control of the Government.' The petitioner violated the above mentioned conditions of the lease agreement, so the allotment was cancelled. No provisions were made in the lease deed that the petitioner will complete the construction work after electric connection, road construction and gas connection. So the plea of failure to complete the construction work is not related with the cancellation of allotment. The petitioner upon misleading the court obtained Rule and stay from the Hon'ble High Court Division. 

 46. The writ petitioner filed Affidavit-in-reply on 18.5.2010 against respondent No.1 and denied the statement and assertion made in the affidavit-in-opposition and stated that failure to complete the construction work within the time stipulated in the contract cannot be a ground for cancellation of the settlement because as per clause (43) of the revised Policy of the settlement of khan land for Hotel/Motel Zone, the respondent No.1 vide Memo No. ভূমঃ/শা-৮/খাজব/২৬৮/৯৭/৫৯৬ dated 20.08.2002 adopted the policy for extension of time for a further period of two years. So, time is not the essence in the Agreement because of having provision for extension of time and cancellation of the settlement is liable to be declared as without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Clause (43) of the Revised Policy of the settlement of Khas land for Hotel/Motel Zone (vide Memo No. ভূমঃ/শা-৮/খাজব/২৬৮/৯৭/৫৯৬ dated 20.08.2002) is her by quoted below: 

 48. In W.P. No. 8638 of 2009 it has been stated that the petitioner got the allotment of Khas land in Cox's Bazar Hotel/Motel zone area under Khatian No. 1, measuring land of 1.12 acre in Dag No. 20001, 0.88 acre of land in Dag No. 20002 on payment of Tk. 61,37.870.50 for construction of Hotel. Respondent No. 5 issued a letter of allotment on 03.03.2003. 

 99. In W.P. No. 1186 of 2010 it has been stated that in response to the advertisement published by the respondent No. 3, the petitioner applied for obtaining settlement a plot measuring 1.00 acres of land on 06.11.2002 for the purpose of constructing a 3 star hotel in the Hotel/Motel Zone of the Cox's Bazar as per the terms and conditions of the revised policy for settlement of Khas land in the Hotel/Motel Zone of Cox's Bazar dated 20.08.2002. The respondent No. 4 opened a long term settlement Case being No.14/2002-2003. 

 124. Another decision on the Case of Government of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh and others Vs. Khashru Miah reported in 58 DLR (AD) 46 paragraph 10. 

 "10. We have heard and considered the submissions. On perusal of the impugned judgment, we find that learned Judges of the High Court Division having meticulously considered the case of the parties, the provisions of Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984 and also considered the decisions of the superior Court and thus came to the finding that the settlements granted in favour of the writ-petitioner respondent Khasru Mia and Ratullah along with others were cancelled without giving theM any notice to show cause for alleged infringement of the terms and conditions of such a lease. Admittedly, the writ-petitioner-respondents were granted settlement by the writ petition respondent No.1 by registered instrument and as such the writ petitioners were legally entitled to be heard before any cancellation of the settlement for the alleged violation of terms and conditions of the lease deed. In the instant case, we find that the learned Judges of the High Court Division upon meticulous consideration as well as on the basis of materials on record held that no prior notice was given to the writ petitioners and along with others before cancellation of the registered deed of settlement. We are fully in agreement with the findings and decisions arrived at by the High Court Division. For all the above reasons, we find no substance in these two petitions. Accordingly, these are dismissed." 

 128. In W.P. No. 8635 of 2009 it has been stated that the petitioner got an allotment of khas land in Cox's Bazaar Hotel/Motel Zone area under khatian No.1, measuring land of 1.73 acre in Dag No.20001, 0.07 acre of land in Dag No.20002 and 0.20 acre in Dag No.20004 on payment of Tk.61,37,870.50 for construction of Hotel. Respondent No.5 issued a letter of allotment on 01.03.2003 vide Memo No.ভুম/শা-৮/খাজব/১৩/২০০৩/১৪৬/১. 

 137. The allottee deposited the entire money to the government and permanent settlement Case No. 18/2002-2003 was started and a lease deed for leasing out of non agricultural Khas land was executed and registered on 06.09.2005 by respondent No. 1 before Sadar Sub-Registrar Cox's Bazar. The name of the allottee has been mutated vide mutation Khatian No. 4615 dated 20.06.2006. The allottee has been paying development tax and Rent. The possession, accordingly, handed over to the allottee by the respondents on 20.06.2006. 

 154. Accordingly, permanent settlement case No.29/2002-2003 was started and a lease deed for leasing out of non-agricultural khas land was executed and registered on 25.01.2004 by respondent No.1 at Sadar Sub-Registrar Office, Cox's Bazar. 

 162. In W.P. No. 551 of 2010 it has been stated that the petitioner filed application to the Deputy Commissioner Cox's bazaar (Respondent No.3) for long term lease of 2.00 acres of non agricultural land (khas land) for the construction of 3 (three) Star Hotel near Cox's Bazaar Sea Beach on 01.02.1994 but the authority allotted 1.00 acre of land to the petitioner for establishing a 3 (three) Star Hotel through long term settlement Case No.31 of 2002-2003. 

 226. In W.P. No. 8639 of 2009 it has been stated that the petitioner got the allotment of khas land in Cox's Bazaar Hotel/Motel Zone area under khatian No.1, measuring land of 0.12 acre in Dag No.20002, 1.62 acre of land in Dag No.20003 and 0.26 acre in Dag No.20004 on payment of Tk.61,37,870.50 for construction of Hotel. Respondent No.5 issued a letter of allotment on 27.02.2003. 

 229. Accordingly, the petitioner deposited the entire money to the government. Then permanent settlement case No.05/2002-2003 was started and a lease deed for leasing out of non-agricultural khas land was executed and registered on 29.02.2004 by respondent No.1 at Sadar Sub-Registrar Office, Cox's Bazaar vide deed No.472. 

 278. The respondent No.4 sent the said plan of the petitioner to the respondent No.2 for necessary action dated 11.6.2005 and the same was accordingly, received by the respondent No.2 on 14.6.2005 and the respondent No.2 under Memo dated 26.6.2005 signed by the Senior Assistant Secretary requested the respondent No.4 to submit a fresh plan as per Rules V of the amended Rules for Allotment of Khas Land for Hotel/Motel, 2002. 

 286. It has been further stated that the petitioner as allottee has not violated any terms and conditions of the letter of allotment and also any rule of the Allotment of Khas Land for Hotel / Motel, 2002 and the petitioner make representation in several occasions before the respondents for issuing No Objection Certificate of plan and execute lease deed but the respondents in no occasion neither issued the No Objection Certificate nor execute lease deed for the allotted land of the petitioner. 

 289. Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner has taken us through the writ petition and Annexure to the writ petition and submitted that the respondents were quite unmindful in issuing the impugned order directing the Deputy Commissioner respondent No.3 to take possession of the plot but in fact the respondent No.3 has not yet accepted the salami, and executed the lease deed and handed over the possession and as such, the question of cancellation of lease deed and taking possession does not arise at all and as such the impugned order dated 12.1.2010 issued by the respondent No.3 is liable to be declared to have issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 290. Mr. Khasru has extraneously submitted that the petitioner acted on the promise of the respondents but the respondent without accepting the salami, and execution of lease deed and handing over possession has issued the impugned memo which on the face of it is illegal and has made without lawful authority and as such the impugned order being bye product of malice in fact and malice in law. The learned Advocate further contends that since no agreement has been executed the question of violation of any terms does not arise and as such the Rule is liable to be absolute. 

 292. Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru to support his contention has referred the decision in the case of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK) Vs. Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority and others reported in 14 BLC paragraph 7, 8 and 9:-

No. 583 of 2010 it has been stated that in consideration of a proposal made by the Deputy commissioner, Cox's Bazar upon an application of the petitioner under Memo dated 27.5.2003 the respondent No. 1 the Ministry of Land had approved the proposal of the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar to give long term Lease to the petitioner of an area of 1.00 acre khas land in the Hotel/Motel Zone in khatian No.1 Plot No.2002, Vide Memo dated 25-05-2004.
